video_title: Jalen Duren re-signs with Pistons, Stephen Curry and Jamal Shead extensions, and another Hield trade

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's five-year, $200 million extension with the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Duren has agreed to re-sign with the Pistons for five years, $200 million.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: After long negotiation, Jalen Duren has agreed to re-sign with the Pistons for five years, $200 million. This was the same reported offer that they had on the table earlier this week or last week. It seems like the last few weeks they kept upping their offer. It is fully guaranteed, no options.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I think the deal is fine. I think it's appropriate given the level of player that he is.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons' negotiation strategy regarding Jalen Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: You have to do whatever it takes to convince the team you're with to have your rights.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: The point is you have to do whatever it takes to convince the team you're with to have your rights, that you're going to take that qualifying offer. It seems like they accomplished that. I'm sure there were agents and young players that are approaching their first rookie scale extension negotiations that hope that Duren would have taken the qualifying offer, because if he did, that would have been such a major shock disruption to the system.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: The Pistons didn't seem to read the room as well as I think they should have. Duren's camp did not have the leverage to get a bump from the 180-190 figure that we'd been hearing for most of the off-season.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Jalen Duren's contract to Alperen Sengun's deal
quotes.excerpt: It's right in the vein of the Alperen Sengun contract, which was five years, $37 million a year.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I think the deal is fine. It's right in the vein of the Alperen Sengun contract, which was five years, $37 million a year, five years, $40 million a year two years later. It's roughly around what the equivalent would have been. Sengun didn't get the biggest annual raises, and I think in the last year or two of that deal, he doesn't get raises at all. So I think Duren will start a little bit lower than Sengun did, or right around where Sengun did, and then obviously end up higher.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I think the qualifying offer thing is a fallacy because yes, on one hand, the Pistons did increase their offer to make it so he would make the same amount of money in five years as if he took the qualifying offer and signed a max with another team next year. But that just, okay, you make the same amount of money in five years, but in the overall arc in his career, that's I don't know, $25 million or so that he wouldn't get back.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Historical rarity of players accepting the qualifying offer
quotes.excerpt: There are seven of them, or at least seven former first-round picks. It's Alex Len, Nerlens Noel, Rodney Hood, Denzel Valentine, Miles Bridges, Cam Thomas, and Quentin Grimes.
quotes.quote: I've got all the list of players since 2018 in front of me who have taken the qualifying offer. There are seven of them, or at least seven former first-round picks. There are scenarios where non-first-round picks have qualifying offers. It's Alex Len, Nerlens Noel, Rodney Hood, Denzel Valentine, Miles Bridges, Cam Thomas, and Quentin Grimes. None of those guys really did well out of that. Quentin Grimes, I guess, is the one maybe exception you could point out. He gets the four years, $60 million from the Lakers, but the Sixers offered him more on an annual basis just on a shorter deal.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' off-season salary management and roster depth
quotes.excerpt: All the salary dumps that they did between Isaiah Stewart, Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser, it was building up to the possibility of them needing to give Duren a big first-year salary.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: All the salary dumps that they did between Isaiah Stewart, Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser, it was building up to the possibility of them needing to give Duren a big first-year salary. And again, I just feel like in the this was the front office's first real test because when they inherited the team, they mostly just kept the same team. They haven't made like a big move, they haven't made a consolidation trade with draft picks. This was their first real test, how do they negotiate with these two core players? And I know I'm in the minority, but I feel that they gave Ausar Thompson and Duren the higher end outcome for both their contract negotiations.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: The Pistons didn't seem to read the room as well as I think they should have. Duren's camp did not have the leverage to get a bump from the 180-190 figure that we'd been hearing for most of the off-season.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Restricted free agency dynamics and team leverage
quotes.excerpt: If he has another playoffs like he had in 2026, his trade value plummets and suddenly look at this contract as a bad contract.
quotes.quote: If he has another playoffs like he had in 2026, his trade value plummets and suddenly look at this contract as a bad contract. And the reason the Lakers made the determination that they made, that they would rather pursue Walker Kessler and even throw a bunch of draft picks at Utah to get him at a slightly lower number than to just give Jalen Duren a max offer sheet, was again, most teams look at their center and they say, we have to get high-level rim protection out of this player because we're not getting it out of anybody else that we have, or most of our other players anyway.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's contract compared to other centers
quotes.excerpt: If you look at who the max centers are, Domantas Sabonis is just overpaid, whatever it is, whatever it is, they're bad contracts.
quotes.quote: If you look at who the max centers are, Domantas Sabonis is just overpaid, whatever it is, whatever it is, they're bad contracts. Anthony Davis and Joel Embiid were max-level players when they signed. They just got older and they got hurt. Nikola Jokic, obviously, pure max-level guy, no question there. Chet Holmgren, Bam Adebayo, I'm forgetting one other name, Karl-Anthony Towns. Those guys are just better, or were better at the time that they signed, than Duren and Sengun were, who I think are even though they're different players, in sort of a similar class.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: The trend of All-Star players receiving maximum rookie scale extensions
quotes.excerpt: Typically, yes, every single All-Star gets an auto-max. The only exception has been Kristaps Porzingis.
quotes.quote: Typically, yes, every single All-Star gets an auto-max. The only exception has been Kristaps Porzingis, but that's because he got injured and then he ended up getting a max, like Jalen Duren, he got it in restricted free agency, right? And it was after he got traded, yeah. So, and then he ended up getting a max. So, very interesting career path between both he and Duren. Have some parallels with using the qualifying offer as a threat, and then ended up getting, well not, Duren didn't get a max, but Porzingis did get a max with the Mavs.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of restricted free agency on team roster building
quotes.excerpt: I do think restricted free agency is going to play a bigger part in this moving forward.
quotes.quote: I do think restricted free agency is going to play a bigger part in this moving forward. I think you look at a team like the Clippers that has max cap space next off-season and it's so destitute with all of those picks lost from the Kawhi investigation. If Jalen Duren had made unrestricted free agency next off-season, or if Jalen Duren had been a restricted free agent next off-season, they would have thrown the max at him.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential trade fit between the Jazz and Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: Something with Utah where it's Lauri Markkanen for Jalen Duren makes a lot of sense for both sides.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: Something with Utah where it's Lauri Markkanen for Jalen Duren makes a lot of sense for both sides. If you're Utah, because you have Jarred Vanderbilt as a power forward who can protect the rim at an elite level and make threes, you're kind of the perfect destination for a player like Jalen Duren.

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: I think that's the cleanest basketball fit. Every other trade that I can think of, I have some pretty significant objection.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Warriors' salary cap situation and potential for future moves
quotes.excerpt: I think it's just an extended expensive retirement tour for Steph. It's not going to be one year.
quotes.quote: I think it's just an extended expensive retirement tour for Steph. It's not going to be one year, like it usually is. It's going to be several years where every year is like, oh, maybe now's the time we do something, and they never will. I think they're self-tanking. Like, obviously you can't really tank in this era. I think they look at their team and they're like, we are just good enough where, assuming Steph misses the number of games he missed last year, we'll be like the seventh-worst team and we'll have the best lottery odds, and we can do that for two or three years while we're paying Steph and Draymond a lot of money to ride out the end of their career, and then they'll retire and we'll have a young team that we can kind of start to build around.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Shead's contract extension with the Raptors
quotes.excerpt: Jamal Shead extended with the Raptors today, three years, $24 million, team option year three.
quotes.quote: Jamal Shead extended with the Raptors today, three years, $24 million, team option year three. Basically the exact same contract Trade Jones got and Trey Mann got with the Trade Jones. Yeah, Trade Jones. Yeah, Trade Jones. They each got last year, so like pretty that seems to be like the standard for like good high-end backup point guard money, $8 million a year. I think Shead's a little better than those guys, so yeah, it seems like a pretty solid deal.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' roster strategy and potential for future trades
quotes.excerpt: If they're going to get Jamal Shead, then they're going to have to do some other moves to make the roster.
quotes.quote: If they're going to get Jamal Shead, then they're going to have to do some other moves to make the roster a little more cohesive, and that would probably mean moving on from some of the other players and probably getting a an upgrade at the guard or hoping Kingston Fleming is good enough to really help maximize Jamal Shead.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' need for a backup point guard
quotes.excerpt: No, the Raptors are the team that need him least in the league.
quotes.quote: No, the Raptors are the team that need him least in the league. Yeah, but I'm sure the Raptors will like him, will want him, and I think the Raptors have players the Pistons would would genuinely like.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' potential interest in a trade for Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: If they're going to get Jalen Duren, then they're going to have to do some other moves.
quotes.quote: If they're going to get Jalen Duren, then they're going to have to do some other moves to make the roster a little more cohesive, and that would probably mean moving on from some of the other players and probably getting a an upgrade at the guard or hoping Kingston Fleming is good enough to really help maximize Jalen Duren.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' potential interest in trading for a center
quotes.excerpt: I think the Raptors will like him, will want him, and I think the Raptors have players.
quotes.quote: I think the Raptors will like him, will want him, and I think the Raptors have players the Pistons would genuinely like. I don't know if they really need him, but they have Jakob Poeltl at this point, now that they have locked up Ausar. But I'm sure the Raptors are going to be in trade rumors, I think, no matter what come January.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' trade assets and potential for a center upgrade
quotes.excerpt: They're the team that need him least in the league.
quotes.quote: They're the team that need him least in the league. Yeah, but I'm sure the Raptors will like him, will want him, and I think the Raptors have players the Pistons would genuinely like. I don't know if they really need him, but they have Jakob Poeltl at this point, now that they have locked up Ausar. But I'm sure the Raptors are going to be in trade rumors, I think, no matter what come January.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren is the primary trade candidate for the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: He's the obvious trade candidate on that team and if he goes into free agency next off-season
quotes.quote: He's the obvious trade candidate on that team and if he goes into free agency next off-season, I think it's lower than the current number. I don't think there's a team out there that's eager to pay RJ Barrett 25 million a year. It's more of a status extension if he gets one and I don't think the Raptors can afford to be giving out status extensions.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Hornets traded Buddy Hield to save money and reduce dead money
quotes.excerpt: The Hornets traded Buddy Hield for Rob Dillingham just to save some money
quotes.quote: The Hornets traded Buddy Hield for Rob Dillingham just to save some money and by doing this they got to reduce the dead money that they would have. So instead of cutting Dorian Finney-Smith at 14 million or Hield at 9 million, they bring in Dillingham cutting at 7 million. Not surprised that they cut Dillingham so early, but just still surreal that this happened so quickly for a guy with the eighth pick two years ago.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Dillingham's NBA career should not be considered over
quotes.excerpt: I think there is enough there that like if somebody gave him a standard contract I wouldn't be terribly surprised
quotes.quote: It's been a very tough two years for him considering where he was drafted. I think there is enough there that like if somebody gave him a standard contract I wouldn't be terribly surprised. I think there's something in there. I don't know if it's enough that he's ever going to be like a consistent rotation player. I don't think his NBA career should be over.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Memphis Grizzlies have a roster issue with too many guards
quotes.excerpt: The one team that came to mind who I think is pretty solid was reclamation project recently is Memphis
quotes.quote: The one team that came to mind who I think is pretty solid was reclamation project recently is Memphis, but they just have such a roster issue as it is. They already have some guards that they would like to probably get on standard contracts, but that's going to take some time as they figure things out on their standard slots. So I'm sure he'll get something. Nembhard though, the other waived Hornet with the Nuggets, you were saying that that might be the best move of the Nuggets off-season potentially?

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Denver Nuggets badly needed another ball-handler like Ryan Nembhard
quotes.excerpt: I guess DeMar DeRozan is such a good player that getting him for the minimum is a very good deal
quotes.quote: I guess DeMar DeRozan is such a good player that getting him for the minimum is a very good deal. But I really like Nembhard, like they badly needed more ball-handling and like Nembhard had real games last year. As far as two-ways go, is he immediately the best two-way player in the NBA? I don't know enough about the rookies to really say that, but among the guys who were on two-ways last year, all the ones who I think were better than him graduated to standard contracts.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Nembhard is a top-tier two-way player candidate
quotes.excerpt: I'll tell you what the answer is yes because I spent like a good 10 minutes trying to decipher
quotes.quote: I'll tell you what the answer is yes because I spent like a good 10 minutes trying to decipher if there are teams that make sense to claim him. I haven't done that with any other waved player this off-season. But in the context of the Nuggets, all they really did was sign minimum guys and then re-sign Spencer Jones to that taxpayer mid-level deal. So if you're talking about all their minimum/two-way deals, yeah, that Nembhard one as of now seems like it would rate among the highest.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Buddy Hield is safe on the Bulls but likely to be traded
quotes.excerpt: I thought he might get cut just whether it was with the Hawks or the Hornets
quotes.quote: I thought he might get cut just whether it was with the Hawks or the Hornets. And I think he's safe for now. He should have a role on the Bulls, but I figure he'll also has a very high probability of getting traded again by the trade deadline. Just because it's kind of like the Dennis Schroder contract where that his contract is just like this sweet spot of well, it doesn't hurt us, but he's also just not doing quite well enough for we need to hold on for him.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Bulls need Buddy Hield's shooting to space the floor
quotes.excerpt: I just hope the Bulls keep him like they just need shooting
quotes.quote: I just hope the Bulls keep him like they just need shooting. It's not like you're going to need him to play a major role, but you know, over the course of a season, especially if you're building around Modestas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson, like two really athletic forwards, you want to have as much shooting around those guys as possible. I see no reason not to just keep them. I mean the Blazers last year had the worst shooting in the in the league.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Buddy Hield's contract structure makes him an expiring deal
quotes.excerpt: He has this non-guaranteed player option like Kristaps Porzingis that I showed earlier
quotes.quote: He has this non-guaranteed player option like Kristaps Porzingis that I showed earlier where if he picks up the option he's guaranteed for like 3.1 million. However, his contract was written in a way where if he is waived before the period in which he has the ability to opt in or out, and for him it's in June, or like basically whenever a season's over through the end of June, which is what how it is 99% of time for players, if he is waived before that, which means he's waived this season, then he doesn't have the opportunity to pick up his option, in which case he doesn't get any partial guarantee.
